title: Sign in to the company's own address and map the person to the company
description: CURRENT method (owner decision via the PM, 2026-11-21): the person opens the company's own address (https://<company>.letflow.qa.bizdala.com). The page asks the server which company the address belongs to, is redirected to that company's own sign-in realm, signs in there and returns to the company address; the server then maps the token to a user and the memberships of that company only. Path 1 browser; path 2 phone app (PWA/APK) with a STORED COMPANY CODE (not an address); path 3 e-mail-first lookup: NOT ENABLED (web build flag VITE_EMAIL_FIRST_LOGIN is off, web/.env.example:30, web/src/auth/emailFirstFlag.ts:13; server mount LetflowLoginDiscovery enabled only outside prod, config/config.exs:123, deploy/.env.example:37 LETFLOW_LOGIN_DISCOVERY_ENABLED empty; its security row is BP-PLATFORM-19); path 4 security cases. No new login features (name@company, company chooser) are in this entry: they are on the later list.
preconditions: the company exists and is active with a host name and a sign-in realm
the user exists in the company (or holds a pending first-administrator grant)

forms: /login (only with the e-mail-first flag; otherwise no screen: ProtectedRoute redirects at once)
tasks.result: PATH 1a, host to company: with no company code known the page asks by host (?host=); a company code in the address (?realm=) or stored in the tab (sessionStorage bpm_realm_slug) wins. A known active company with a realm answers its own sign-in realm, client id, branding and type; an unknown host, the bare host and no parameter answer the same default body (200, never an error); the answer is not cached after a failed read (tenantConfig.ts:96).

PATH 1b, unknown company code: an explicit code that names no company never reaches the identity provider; the page shows the company-not-found screen (web/src/auth/CompanyNotFound.tsx) and forgets the code.

PATH 1c, redirect: the page redirects to the company's realm (authority from the config) with the return address <company address>/auth/callback (the realm slug is embedded when a code was used, so the callback finds the realm).
PATH 1d, return: the callback exchanges the code (signinRedirectCallback), keeps the user in memory only (OidcManager.ts:32, InMemoryWebStorage) and opens the saved page of the company address.

PATH 1e, session: the token is renewed 60 s before it expires (refresh token first, hidden frame as fallback); a failed renewal that the API client's 401 path cannot repair raises 'auth:session-expired': the session is cleared, a notice is kept and the person is sent to the same realm to sign in again. The session is not kept across a page reload (memory store).

PATH 1f, token to company: the server verifies the token, takes the company from the REALM of the token (iss /realms/<slug>), checks that the realm belongs to that company and maps the person; the address (Host) is not read on any /api/v1 route, so the company of a request is the token's. The answer is the person's own roles, permissions and user id.
the person's memberships of this company are listed (this company only).

tasks.actor: any user (phone app, PWA or APK)
tasks.result: PATH 2, phone app: the app is NOT given a company address. It sends one server (build-time LETFLOW_API_BASE_URL, api_client.dart:395) the COMPANY CODE the person typed (?slug=); a known company answers its realm (company_found true), an unknown code answers the default body with company_found false and the app stops (tenantNotFound). After sign-in through the native OIDC library the app stores a pointer {realm_url, slug} of the last active company (LastActiveTenantPointer, written by writeLastActiveTenant) and the refresh token under that code, and reopens into that company.
PATH 3, e-mail-first lookup: NOT ENABLED today (flags above). One line only; its uniform answers are the security row BP-PLATFORM-19.

inputs: credential (OIDC token) of the company's realm
refusals: unknown host, bare host, no parameter, unknown company code: the same default 200 body, no error and no hint which part failed (anti-oracle; SEC-ID-01, BP-TENANT-ADMIN-42); the logo of an unknown code is the plain 404

no or malformed Authorization header: 401 'missing or malformed Authorization header'; wrong, expired or unsigned token, unknown realm: 401 'invalid or expired bearer token' (auth_pipeline.ex:213-225; BP-TENANT-ADMIN-37)

a token of another company's realm: the company of the request is the token's, so the person of company A at company B's address sees A's own data only; an id of company B read by A answers the plain 404 'the requested resource was not found', identical to an id that does not exist (SEC-ID-02, BP-TENANT-ADMIN-43; this entry's scenario steps s5-s7). The server does NOT refuse by host: no /api/v1 plug reads the Host header (grep tenant_by_hostname in lib: only tenant_config.ex)
a realm that is not bound to the token's company: 401 'token realm does not match tenant' (auth_pipeline.ex:228)
a deactivated company: 403 tenant_inactive (auth_pipeline.ex:213)

no secret and no user existence in any answer: the public config carries only realm, client id, branding, type and env label (tenant_config.ex response allowlist); there is no per-user lookup in this process
browser_evidence: The operator's real-browser check of 2026-11-21 22:54 (headless Chromium): the sign-in at the company address, redirect to the company realm and return, OK for all three QA tenants (the three QA tenants named in the operator record of that check, which is not in the repository). Playwright in web/tests/e2e covers only parts: oidcf2-subdomain.e2e.spec.ts (host to realm; the navigation to the identity provider is aborted, no return), oidcf-login.e2e.spec.ts and iss-0726-oidc-deep-link-restore.e2e.spec.ts (deep-link restore). GAP: no test in web/tests/e2e plays the full redirect, sign-in and return on a company host in CI.
gaps: browser redirect and return on a company host: no CI test (see browser_evidence); phone app path: needs a device or emulator, the runner cannot play it (written reason); no 'no credential' or 'crafted credential' runner step kind: BP-TENANT-ADMIN-37 gap

Runner scripts: SEC-ID-03 (BP-TENANT-ADMIN-44) and SEC-ID-07 play the roles TENANT_ADMIN and STOREKEEPER on the routes whose path the static check can match; the storekeeper is refused every one with 403.

Read-only parts of the same router are in SEC-ID-07 (integrity and token preconditions: administrator 200, storekeeper 403).

title: SECURITY: Token and host lookup: wrong, expired, other-realm credential and unknown host
description: A request without a credential, with a wrong or expired token, or with a token of another company, and a request to an unknown or inactive host, are refused with identical answers and nothing is changed.
preconditions: an expired token, a token of another company, an unknown host name

tasks.result: protected read
public configuration of an unknown or inactive company

inputs: credential of the actor named in each task
refusals: 401 for a missing or invalid credential
the not-found answer for an unknown or inactive host (no hint about which part failed)
gaps: A missing, malformed or expired credential needs a request without the actor's token: the runner always sends the token of the named actor (no 'no credential' or 'crafted credential' step kind). A token of another company is played by SEC-ID-02 (BP-TENANT-ADMIN-43) and the host and realm lookup by SEC-ID-01 (BP-TENANT-ADMIN-42). The tenant-config routes are answered by host before sign-in and have no actor.

The sign-in entry BP-TENANT-ADMIN-01 plays the mapping of a token to its own company and the other company's token at this address (scenario BP-TENANT-ADMIN-01-sign-in-company-address); the host is not a refusal criterion (the server does not read it on /api/v1).

title: SECURITY: Approval and separation of duties negatives
description: Self-approval is tried with the switch ON, with an API token and a service principal with the switch OFF, and a rule switch is tried by a non-administrator and by a token.
preconditions: a process step with distinct_from

tasks.result: complete a step that must be done by another person
switch the rule

title: SECURITY: Crafted request bodies: unknown keys, tenant ids and write targets
description: Bodies with unknown keys, a foreign tenant_id or crafted fields are refused or ignored; refusals write nothing and echo no submitted value.
preconditions: signed in as TENANT_ADMIN

tasks.result: settings with out-of-scope keys

The crafted-body targets PATCH /tenant/settings and POST /tenant/solutions are root routes of their prefix: the runner's static check cannot match a route mounted at the root of a two-part prefix (/tenant/settings, /tenant/scope-enforcement, /tenant/solutions, /tenant/role-grants, /tenant/role-scope-grants), see scripts/uat/check_processes.py Routes.match (a route that is only '/' or only a wildcard gets no literal tail). title: SECURITY: The storekeeper does not hold the stock approve permission; the tenant administrator does (decision 0093)

title: Scroll a long list past a day: the My Tasks inbox
description: A storekeeper or administrator opens My Tasks (the task inbox) on a tenant with a long inbox, some of it older than 24 hours, and scrolls page after page by the cursor the answer gives until there is no next cursor. Every page answers 200, no task appears twice and none is skipped. A cursor must keep working however old the last row of its page is (class of the defect T-2571: the cursor expired by the age of the last row and page 3 answered 410). Read-only; nothing to clean up. The runner script follows the cursor (page_through step), asserts the oldest task is older than 24 hours ('inconclusive: no old rows' otherwise) and that ids are unique across pages.
preconditions: an active tenant with a long inbox: more than one page of tasks and at least one task older than 24 hours (qoimeks-qa2 had more than 400 open tasks on 2026-11-21; read it at run time, do not assume)
the product carries the fix of T-2571 (merged as 9315ba6fa)

tasks.result: each page answers 200 with items, count and next_cursor; the cursor carries the seek key of the last row and its own issue time, so an old last row does not expire it; the last page has next_cursor null

outputs: oldest task age (in the run record)
refusals: a malformed cursor or a cursor of another list answers 422 (the same text for both)
a page size outside the allowed range answers 400
gaps: The stock documents list (GET /api/v1/modules/stock/documents) is not scrolled by this script: the route takes `limit` (not `page_size`; any other key is refused invalid_filter, documents.ex list_filters) and answers `rows` (not `items`), while the runner's page_through step always sends page_size and reads `items` (runner.py _page_through). Needs a runner change (configurable limit parameter and rows key); its cursor carries no expiry (documents.ex cursor_of), so the class of T-2571 does not apply to it.
